# Abstract

This gazetteer compiles 828 catalogued settlements (1.466 settlement-year observations) active across Canada (642), Greenland (182) and Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon (4) between 1500AD and 1763AD under CENTAUR-II. Drawn from *Censuses of Canada 1665 to 1871* Vol. IV, Acadian parish rolls, Hudson's Bay Company and French interior post complements, Pacific and Subarctic archaeological syntheses and Danish-Moravian Greenland mission and calibrated Indigenous winter-settlement records [@statcan1876censuses; @ray1974indians; @boyd1999coming; @gad1973history], the catalogue spans all eight regional masks: New France St. Lawrence (294), Greenland (182), Rupert's Land (95), Pacific Northwest Coast, Yukon and Mackenzie (84), Acadia and Nova Scotia (76), Newfoundland, Labrador and Saint-Pierre (65), Pays d'en Haut (17) and Western Prairies (15). Leading centres prior to the 1763AD Treaty of Paris were Québec (9k in 1750-1759AD), Montréal (6k in 1750AD), Louisbourg (5,2k in 1758AD), Halifax (4k in 1755AD; 3k in 1763AD), Grand-Pré (2,5k in 1750AD), St. John's (2,4k in 1763AD), Île d'Orléans (2,25k in 1739AD), Beaubassin (1,6k in 1755AD), Pisiguit (1,6k in 1750AD), Lunenburg (1.453 in 1753AD), Marpole (1,45k in 1500AD) and Port-Royal (1,45k in 1752AD) [@statcan1876censuses; @boyd1999coming]. Alongside the 828 included records, the source ledger documents 116 deduplicated exclusions (944 total candidates, 0 unaccounted).

# Background

Before 1763AD, nucleated settlement in northern North America divided between Indigenous villages anchored to marine and riverine resources and European colonial towns concentrated along three eastern corridors. Along the St. Lawrence seigneurial axis, French parishes and fortified towns ran continuously between Québec, Trois-Rivières and Montréal; in the Maritimes, Acadian dyked marshlands at Port-Royal, Grand-Pré and Beaubassin coexisted with the French fortress port of Louisbourg and British Halifax; and across eastern Newfoundland, English and French winter fishing stations occupied St. John's, Plaisance, Carbonear and Harbour Grace [@statcan1876censuses; @prins1996mikmaq].

Across the interior shield, prairies and Pacific Northwest, permanent Hudson's Bay Company coastal factories (York Factory, Churchill, Moose Factory and Fort Albany) and French *Pays d'en Haut* posts held modest winter complements amidst much larger Indigenous towns and riverine habitation hubs such as Marpole, Yuquot, Kittigazuit, Laxgalts'ap, Lockport and Estipah-skikikini-kots [@ray1974indians; @trigger1985natives; @boyd1999coming]. In West and South Greenland, Indigenous Thule winter settlements documented across Disko Bay, Nuup Kangerlua and Avanersuaq joined Danish colonial trading stations and Moravian missions founded from Nuuk (1721/1728AD) to Ilulissat and Paamiut [@gad1973history].

# Methodology

All 828 settlement entries carry CENTAUR provenance and snap onto the eight 5-arcminute regional masks using a 14-pixel coastal search radius so peninsular outports, islands and Greenlandic fjords assign cleanly to their parent mask. Greenlandic Danish colonial names (Godthåb, Jakobshavn, Julianehåb) were standardised to Kalaallisut headwords (Nuuk, Ilulissat, Qaqortoq) with Danish exonyms retained as alternative names, and pre-1721 Indigenous Greenland sites inherit archaeologically calibrated fjord-settlement trajectories bounded safely within Greenland's 7k early modern population ceiling [@gad1973history]. Every settlement observation falls strictly within the 1500AD to 1763AD chronological domain.

Ledger deduplication consolidates 116 duplicate alias candidate entries out of 944 total candidates within a 2 km matching radius into canonical settlement keys, unifying colonial and Indigenous aliases such as Port-Royal Acadia, Grand-Pré, Quebec Capital, Montreal City, Sainte-Famille-de-l'Île-d'Orléans, Placentia, Windsor-ON, Saint-Gervais, Sermermiut (into Ilulissat), Asummiut (into Sisimiut), Nuuk Colony (into Nuuk) and Miquelon (into Miquelon Settlement).

# Testing and Validation

Ledger reconciliation confirms 828 included settlements and 116 excluded duplicate or alias entries (944 total candidates, 0 unaccounted). All 828 records pass WGS84 coordinate bounds, mask containment and positive integer population checks across 1.466 settlement-year observations (1,77 observations per settlement on average). Figure \ref{fig:sett-cc1763} plots the 828-settlement rank-size distribution alongside the fifteen largest peaks.

# Results

## Top 45 Settlements by Peak Population

Table \ref{tab:gazetteer-cc1763} lists the Top 45 catalogued settlements ranked descending by peak population within the 1500AD to 1763AD window, reporting regional territory, WGS84 coordinates, active chronological span and benchmark populations at 1681AD, 1739AD and 1763AD.

```{r tab-gazetteer, results='asis'}
fmt_coord <- function(x) gsub("\\.", ",", format(round(as.numeric(x), 2), nsmall = 2, trim = TRUE))
get_pop_str <- function(e, y) {
  v <- e$population[[y]]
  if (is.null(v)) return("-")
  viscount_fmt_pop(v)
}

peaks <- vapply(sett_data, function(e) max(unlist(e$population)), numeric(1))
ord <- order(peaks, decreasing = TRUE)
top_n <- min(45L, length(ord))

rows <- lapply(sett_data[ord[seq_len(top_n)]], function(e) {
  yrs <- as.integer(names(e$population))
  pk_y <- names(e$population)[which.max(unlist(e$population))]
  pk_v <- max(unlist(e$population))
  reg_nm <- mod_data$regions[[e$region_id]]$name
  reg_short <- sub("^[0-9]+\\.\\s*", "", reg_nm)
  reg_short <- sub(":.*$", "", reg_short)
  reg_short <- sub("\\s*\\(.*$", "", reg_short)
  data.frame(
    Settlement = e$name,
    Region = gsub("&", "and", reg_short, fixed = TRUE),
    Coords = paste0(fmt_coord(e$coords[[1]]), ", ", fmt_coord(e$coords[[2]])),
    Span = paste0(min(yrs), "-", max(yrs)),
    P1681 = get_pop_str(e, "1681"),
    P1739 = get_pop_str(e, "1739"),
    P1763 = get_pop_str(e, "1763"),
    Peak = paste0(viscount_fmt_pop(pk_v), " (", pk_y, ")"),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
})
gaz_df <- do.call(rbind, rows)
rownames(gaz_df) <- NULL

viscount_table(
  gaz_df,
  "Top 45 settlements in Colonial Canada and Greenland to 1763AD ordered by peak catalogued population.",
  c("Settlement", "Region", "Lat, Lon", "Span", "1681AD", "1739AD", "1763AD", "Peak (Year)"),
  list(label = "tab:gazetteer-cc1763", font_size = "scriptsize", max_rows_per_page = 32L)
)
```

## Sub-Regional Gazetteer Distribution

Table \ref{tab:regsum-cc1763} summarises site counts and leading centres across all eight regional masks. All eight sub-regions now carry catalogued nuclei, led in site count by New France St. Lawrence (294) and Greenland (182) and in peak settlement size by Québec (9k), Montréal (6k), Louisbourg (5,2k) and Marpole (1,45k) [@statcan1876censuses; @boyd1999coming].

```{r tab-regsum, results='asis'}
reg_keys <- names(mod_data$regions)
sum_rows <- lapply(reg_keys, function(rk) {
  sub_e <- Filter(function(e) identical(e$region_id, rk), sett_data)
  max_nm <- "-"
  if (length(sub_e) > 0) {
    pks <- vapply(sub_e, function(e) max(unlist(e$population)), numeric(1))
    idx_m <- which.max(pks)
    max_nm <- paste0(sub_e[[idx_m]]$name, " (", viscount_fmt_pop(pks[idx_m]), ")")
  }
  reg_short <- sub("^[0-9]+\\.\\s*", "", mod_data$regions[[rk]]$name)
  data.frame(
    Region = gsub("&", "and", reg_short, fixed = TRUE),
    Sites = viscount_fmt_number(length(sub_e), 0L),
    Lead = max_nm,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
})
sum_df <- do.call(rbind, sum_rows)
rownames(sum_df) <- NULL

viscount_table(
  sum_df,
  "Settlement counts and leading centres across all eight regional masks to 1763AD (828 total sites).",
  c("Sub-Region", "Sites", "Leading Site (Peak)"),
  list(label = "tab:regsum-cc1763", font_size = "footnotesize")
)
```

## Excluded Candidates and Deduplication Ledger

Table \ref{tab:excluded-cc1763} presents a 25-row sample of the 116 deduplicated candidate entries from the regional source ledger, documenting canonical alias merging and close-proximity consolidation.

```{r tab-excluded, results='asis'}
exc_list <- Filter(function(c) !identical(c$status, "included"), ledger_data$candidates)
exc_ca <- Filter(function(c) identical(c$country, "Canada"), exc_list)
exc_gl <- Filter(function(c) !identical(c$country, "Canada"), exc_list)
exc_sample <- c(exc_ca, exc_gl)
exc_sample <- exc_sample[seq_len(min(25L, length(exc_sample)))]

clean_just <- function(s) {
  out <- gsub("CENTAUR Verified Colonial Registry", "CENTAUR Colonial Registry", s, fixed = TRUE)
  out <- gsub("([0-9]+)\\.([0-9]+)\\s*km", "\\1,\\2 km", out)
  out <- gsub("([0-9])\\s*/\\s*([0-9])", "\\1/\\2", out)
  out <- gsub(" / ", "/", out, fixed = TRUE)
  out
}

exc_rows <- lapply(exc_sample, function(c) {
  data.frame(
    Candidate = c$name,
    Country = c$country,
    Reason = "Duplicate alias or twin",
    Detail = clean_just(c$justification),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
})
exc_df <- do.call(rbind, exc_rows)
rownames(exc_df) <- NULL

viscount_table(
  exc_df,
  "Sample of 25 deduplicated entries from the 116 excluded candidates in the 1500 to 1763AD source ledger.",
  c("Candidate", "Territory", "Category", "Consolidation Detail"),
  list(label = "tab:excluded-cc1763", font_size = "scriptsize", max_rows_per_page = 30L)
)
```

# Limitations

Three constraints govern the 1500 to 1763AD gazetteer. First, sixteenth-century Iroquoian sites such as Stadacona (Québec) and Hochelaga (Montréal) carry contact-era village approximations (1k and 1,5k at 1535AD) rather than formal censuses [@tremblay2006st]. Second, St. Lawrence rural parishes (Beaupré, Île d'Orléans, La Prairie, Boucherville) represent seigneurial parish aggregates rather than compact urban street grids [@statcan1876censuses]. Third, Saint-Pierre and Miquelon fall inside the Newfoundland, Labrador and Saint-Pierre mask prior to 1763AD before receiving a dedicated island mask in the post-1763AD British North American chapter.
